summary: mountainash-rules provides two complementary rule evaluation architectures under core/ + engines/{filter,accumulator}/ that share a unified dimension model and expression system. Both engines are backend-agnostic through the mountainash.relations and mountainash.expressions layers, enabling operation across Polars, Ibis, and Narwhals-backed DataFrames. A rich ternary logic system powers sentinel-aware matching with full observability, and backend purity is enforced package-wide with exactly three documented exceptions.

concepts.name: Shared dimension model
concepts.description: DimensionsMetadata serves as the single source of truth for both engines, with YAML round-trip and table-level hit-policy fields. It encapsulates dimension definitions, match strategies, and sentinel configuration, providing a consistent contract that decouples rule semantics from evaluation strategy.

evidence.detail: DimensionsMetadata: table-level hit_policy/priority_field/output_fields plus YAML round-trip

concepts.name: Filter engine: expression compilation and evaluation
concepts.description: DimensionCompiler translates the 13 MatchStrategy members into BaseExpressionAPI expressions, with the documented Polars-native per-row REGEX exception. ExpressionRulesEngine evaluates the compiled expressions against one context, a batch of contexts, or every rule without survivor filtering through explain(), producing ternary columns, survival and specificity. Strategy-specific sentinel behavior is defined by the compiler rather than a universal unknown branch.

concepts.name: Accumulator engine: prime-encoded combination lattice
concepts.description: Each rule receives a unique prime number as its identity (up to MAX_RULES_PER_PARTITION=10,000 per partition). Rule combinations are represented as the product of their constituent primes, giving every combination a unique fingerprint, bounded to ~15 primes per combination by int64 (LatticeWidthExceededError beyond that). The build phase iteratively expands valid combinations, and a frontier filter prunes dominated entries via modular arithmetic, producing a compact Lattice of all maximal valid combinations.

concepts.name: Ternary partition routing meta-engine
concepts.description: LatticeIndex embeds a meta-engine over EXACT_KEY dimensions to route CONTEXT_KEY-partitioned contexts to the correct lattice using the same ternary + specificity semantics as ordinary rule evaluation, rather than a separate ad hoc dispatch mechanism -- keeping the routing layer consistent with the rest of the architecture.

evidence.detail: LatticeIndex meta-engine over EXACT_KEY dimensions design

concepts.name: Backend-agnostic protocol via mountainash.relations
concepts.description: All DataFrame operations flow through the Relation protocol, which abstracts over concrete backends. relation(df) wraps any supported DataFrame, and collect() materialises results back to the caller's native format. This design allows the same rule definitions and evaluation logic to run on Polars, Ibis, or Narwhals-Pandas backends.

evidence.detail: 'Backend Support' section: Polars, Pandas-via-Narwhals, or Ibis all accepted as `rules`
RuleResult accessors return a DataFrame in the same backend as the input rules

concepts.name: Ternary logic and sentinel-aware expressions
concepts.description: The expression system uses a three-valued logic (match=1, unknown=0, non-match=-1) to handle missing or wildcard rule values gracefully across string, numeric, temporal, bool, and set-typed dimensions. Set-dimension wildcards use an in-band '[sentinel]' list (never null) normalized via core/set_wildcard.py, since bool and set types have no reliable null-as-wildcard convention across backends.

evidence.detail: in-band set-sentinel wildcard design, since bool/set types lack a portable null-as-wildcard convention

concepts.name: Backend purity enforcement and documented exceptions
concepts.description: No module under src/mountainash_rules/ may import polars/ibis/narwhals directly. tests/test_backend_purity.py parametrises every non-dunder module with no exemptions. Exactly three '# allow:' escapes are documented: the per-row REGEX fallback (pending upstream regex_contains column-pattern support), the empty-build schema seed in the accumulator engine (pending backend-agnostic empty-frame support), and the snapshot parquet read in Lattice.load (pending backend-agnostic parquet.read_table).

evidence.detail: parametrised over every non-dunder module, no exemptions
three documented '# allow:' escapes: per-row REGEX fallback, empty-build schema seed, snapshot parquet read

concepts.name: CTX_PREFIX column injection pattern
concepts.description: Context values are bound into the evaluation frame as literal columns with a __ctx_ prefix. The compiler references these prefixed columns by convention, enabling a clean separation between rule metadata columns and runtime context values within a single DataFrame operation.

documentation_plan: Present the shared dimension model and the mountainash.relations backend-agnostic protocol as the architectural foundation before either engine.
Document the filter engine's expression-compilation architecture and the accumulator engine's prime-encoded lattice architecture as parallel, comparable designs.
Cover the ternary partition routing meta-engine and CTX_PREFIX column-injection pattern as implementation patterns layered on top of the base architecture.
Document ternary logic and sentinel-aware expressions once, referenced by both engine sections rather than duplicated.
State backend purity enforcement and its three documented exceptions as an explicit architectural constraint, not an implementation detail.
